description: We’re MISMATCH, a team of two 9th-grade students joining our first NASA challenge! We’re beginners, but we bring curiosity, energy, and a real love of learning. Our theme is EDUCATION: we want to turn space science and NASA data into something fun and easy for students our age to explore. We’re looking for teammates with coding, design, or data skills, or anyone excited to learn with us. Different skills, one shared mission!
summary: Lunar Base Rewind is a first-person lunar base training game designed for children aged 7–12. Players build facilities and balance power, oxygen and food across seven turns while responding to equipment faults, space-weather alerts and delayed supplies. NASA DONKI solar flare, solar energetic particle and coronal mass ejection records shape simplified training conditions. The key feature is rewind: players revisit a decision, try another strategy and compare the outcomes using the same data. This makes engineering trade-offs visible through experimentation. Historical NASA records support offline play and are clearly distinguished from newly fetched records. The prototype aims to make space exploration approachable while encouraging systems thinking, resource planning and learning from mistakes.
details:
Play the browser version: https://lunar-base-rewind.vercel.app/
Use a desktop computer with a keyboard and mouse. No installation or login is required.

Lunar Base Rewind turns lunar base engineering into a playable cycle of building, testing and revising decisions. Designed for children aged 7–12, the prototype asks players to keep a small lunar base operating for seven turns while balancing power, oxygen and food.

Players explore a 5×5 construction area in first person and build or remove facilities at nearby sites. Solar arrays generate power, batteries store surplus energy, habitats support oxygen supply, greenhouses produce food and shelters support responses to space-weather alerts. Limited construction tokens and competing resource demands mean that each choice has consequences. A central terminal provides resource information, forecasts and turn history, while a read-only map helps players understand the base layout.

The main learning feature is rewind. Players can restore an earlier turn, change a decision and compare the results. The NASA data context remains fixed during the run and its rewinds, allowing players to examine the effects of their choices. The intended impact is to encourage systems thinking, planning and learning from mistakes through direct experimentation.

NASA Goddard Space Flight Center’s Community Coordinated Modeling Center provides the DONKI records used by the game. Solar flare class affects protection power requirements, observation-backed solar energetic particle records add a protection requirement, and coronal mass ejection records select a longer delayed-advice exercise. The game attempts a one-time retrieval for each data type at startup and uses archived records from May 8–13, 2024 when data is unavailable. Historical, fetched and mixed data sources are identified explicitly; this is not a continuous live feed.

These mappings are simplified educational rules, not predictions of astronaut radiation exposure, lunar outages or physical communication delays. Canadian Space Agency educational material informs project-written explanations about food production and limited resupply.

The prototype was developed using Godot, GDScript and Blender-authored assets. Short English instructions, icons, resource bars and contextual actions support the intended audience. Local Windows play is available. Evaluation with children and broader browser testing remain future validation work.

AI disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with code implementation, debugging, English interface text, documentation, automated checks and presentation preparation. Original NASA records are retained separately from AI-assisted explanations. The team remains responsible for reviewing the final project and its source attribution.
dataRefs: NASA CCMC DONKI — Solar Flare, Solar Energetic Particle and Coronal Mass Ejection Records
